newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-ANALYSIS OF WIMBLEDON MEN'S SINGLES FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ANALYSIS OF WIMBLEDON MEN'S SINGLES FINAL.

text.p: Analysis of Wimbledon men's singles final on Sunday between Pete Sampras of the United States and Cedric Pioline of France.

Pioline made a nervous start with a double fault first point, and his serve was always under threat from Sampras's whipping returns. The American world number one, who lost only four points against his own serve in the set, broke Pioline in the third game, converting a third break point with a backhand return down the line.

Pioline settled and won his next two service games comfortably but, despite some brilliant flashes such as an exquisite topspin lob and a backhand down the line, he could make no impression on Sampras's defences and the American served out the set 6-4 in 36 minutes.
Sampras broke Pioline's serve again in the fifth game of the second set, his fine returns forcing a string of volley errors from the Frenchman.

Pioline fought back from 15-40 down with two aces in the seventh game. But Sampras's hefty returns told and he lured the Frenchman into more mistakes at the net to break the serve again and go 5-2 up.

Sampras's own thumping delivery remained impenetrable and he lost only two points against it in the set, both in the final game. He broke a string with a punching volley in that game, but came back with a big serve for set point which he converted with a precise volley to win it 6-2.

Pioline started positively, winning the opening game on his serve to love, and then, for the first time in the match put pressure on Sampras's serve. Sampras was twice taken to deuce, but on both occasions he won the next the point with an ace before levelling at 1-1.
The American quickly killed off Pioline's challenge, stealing the third game to love, the Frenchman hashing a backhand volley to give Sampras the break.

They both exchanged two service games, holding easily, before Pioline earned his first break point of the match in the eighth game. Sampras was up to the challenge, however, striking two powerful serves to take the game and build a 5-3 lead.
Sampras served for the match, clinching his fourth Wimbledon title and his 10th Grand Slam trophy with a service winner to take the set 6-4. The match took one hour and 34 minutes.
